findings.description: The inline user policy grants full service-wide wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*", violating least privilege. A compromise of this user's credentials yields full control of compute, storage and serverless resources across the account, including data exfiltration from any S3 bucket and privilege escalation via lambda function creation with attached roles.

A permanent IAM access key is created for a human-less service user rather than using an IAM role with temporary STS credentials. The secret is stored in Terraform state in a recoverable form and never rotates, providing a durable credential for the highly privileged policy attached to this user.

No PGP key is supplied, so the access key secret is stored in plaintext in the Terraform state file (the encrypted_secret attribute is only populated when pgp_key is set). Anyone with read access to state obtains working credentials for the privileged svc_deploy user.

The svc_deploy_key_material output exposes access key secret material and is not marked sensitive, so it is printed to the console and recorded in CI/CD logs and state outputs where it may be read by anyone with pipeline or state access.

A highly privileged IAM user is created with no permissions boundary and no MFA enforcement condition, so the wildcard inline policy has no upper bound and credentials alone are sufficient for full access.
